attrs.evidence: R5.2 stored `status: eliminated` on the defeater and `elimination_refs` beside it — two truth sources for one fact, and the second was checked only for RESOLUTION. That is the R5.1 defect (a reference that resolves is a reference that supports) reproduced one layer up, against doubts instead of against claims, in the round that fixed it for claims. GPT-5.6 reproduced it: point DEF-1PA-REDUCTION-MISMATCH.elimination_refs at FED-Q2-D3-WITNESS, an existential about girth-4 graphs, and a doubt about a polymorphism reduction reads as eliminated with the gate green. Registered as INC-R52-ELIM-UNRELATED and refused by MUT-ELIM-UNRELATED, which runs on every gate invocation.

attrs.note: THE FIRST ACT OF THIS RECORD WAS TO COST THE ARTIFACT ITS ONLY ELIMINATION — and then give it back under a reading. Typing the elimination as an inference gave it a challenge surface, and the honest doubt about it (DEF-ELIM-1PA-IMPL-FIDELITY: that FED-1PA-DEC-IMPL decides the property FED-1PA-CORE names rather than a neighbouring one) was already true and unstated inside the old `elimination_refs` entry. Under the STRICT compilation that open doubt defeats the eliminator and the original doubt reverts to open; under the ELIMINATIVE one it does not. That disagreement is ASR-COMPILE-AF and it is this artifact's first witnessed semantics question.
attrs.prior_art: Goodenough, Weinstock & Klein CMU/SEI-2015-TR-005 — elimination is an inference about a specific doubt. GPT-5.6's adjudication of Fable's R5.2 pass, F1.
attrs.statement: Eliminating a defeater is a typed inference whose conclusion is `elim(D)` for one exact defeater, carrying a declared elimination MODE and support that touches that doubt's own subject. A defeater record may not state that it was eliminated.
